payload.title: PEER_MIN_WRITE_ROUTES (3) and PEER_MIN_CAPABILITY_ROUTES (4) can never change a result because the integer 75 percent share already needs a class of at least four routes before any outlier exists, the numbers are restated as prose in the manifest premises, and no test pins any of the three values.
evidence: tools/aria-adapters/security-boundary-adapter.ts:130-134 (the two minimums and the share comment)
tools/aria-adapters/security-boundary-adapter.ts:379-381 (the share is compared as count times 4 at least total times 3)
tools/aria-adapters/security-boundary-adapter.tool.json:79 (premise says a class with at least three such routes)
tools/aria-adapters/security-boundary-adapter.tool.json:89 (premise says a class with at least four such routes)
tools/aria-adapters/security-boundary-adapter.test.ts:269-283 (the near rows pin the share outcome; the same rows pass with any minimum up to 4)
payload.rule_violated: A threshold must be stated once and pinned (CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach tier 3); a constant that cannot fire and a premise that quotes it misstate what the rule enforces.
payload.notes: With n routes and g guarded, an outlier needs 4g at least 3n and g below n, which first holds at n = 4 with g = 3, so the constants 3 and 4 never exclude a class that the share has not already excluded (setting both to 0 leaves the whole test green, per the review probe). The premise tells the judge 'at least three' while the code can fire only from four, and a later edit of a constant or of the share leaves the contract text the judge reads stale with no test failing. Close condition: Derive the minimum class size from the share (delete the two constants, or raise them above 4 on purpose) and pin the real floor with fixtures at 3 and 4 routes for both rules; make the premise text derive from or be tested against the constants. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 4). Verified at origin/main d716541239.
